title: EPIC 16: Cast-Accuracy Minigame Wiring (CastResult remote)
description:
BACKGROUND: The codebase has TWO separate timing minigames that were both implemented but only ONE was wired end-to-end:

  1. CAST-OVERLAY MINIGAME (client lines 996-1090): Triggered by CastState:FireClient(true, castTime). Shows a marker sweeping across a bar with a green "hit zone". Player clicks to stop it. Fires `CastResult:FireServer(accuracy)`. This measures CAST ACCURACY — did you release at the right moment during the cast windup?

  2. BITE MINIGAME (client lines 1183-1304): Triggered by BiteEvent. Shows a separate ping-pong marker. Player taps to stop it. Fires `SubmitCatchInput({hit=bool})`. This measures REACTION TIMING — did you respond fast enough when the fish bit?

PROBLEM: The cast-overlay minigame was fully built (UI, animation, input handling) but `CastResult` had NO server handler. The accuracy value was fired into the void. Meanwhile, GameConfig.MiniGame.accuracyLuckBonus (perfect=25, good=12, ok=0) was defined but never consumed — a dead config table that was clearly INTENDED to be driven by the cast accuracy.

DESIGN DECISION (user-directed, 2026-07-18): Wire CastResult rather than remove the minigame. The cast-overlay becomes a skill-based luck bonus: a well-timed cast grants a temporary luck boost that improves species rarity on the subsequent catch.

HOW IT WORKS (post-wiring):
  1. Server computes authoritative hit-zone bounds (centered randomly per cast) from RodDefinitions.minigameZoneSize
  2. Server sends bounds + castDeadline to client via CastState
  3. Client renders the zone from server bounds and animates the marker
  4. Player clicks → client sends CastResult with marker position
  5. Server re-derives accuracy tier from marker position vs server-authoritative bounds
  6. Server stores luckBonus on activeBites (consumed by the catch species roll later)

This is NOT the same as the bite minigame's security mitigation (N16's rng:NextNumber > zoneSize check). The cast overlay is a BONUS mechanism, not a gate — you can still catch fish without a good cast, but a good cast shifts the odds.

WHY THIS MATTERS: The fishing loop is the core engagement loop. Right now, casting is a passive wait (castTime delay). The cast-overlay minigame adds active skill expression to the FIRST half of the loop, complementing the bite minigame's reflex test in the second half. This gives players two skill checks per catch instead of one, deepening the moment-to-moment gameplay.

CONSIDERATIONS:
- The server must be authoritative on the hit-zone bounds (not the client) to prevent "always perfect" exploits
- The luckBonus is consumed by FishDefinitions.getRandomInZone's luck parameter, which shifts weights toward rarer species
- accuracyLuckBonus values (25/12/0) are substantial — a "perfect" cast adds 25 luck, equivalent to a Golden Rod (20) + Magic Bait (15) combined. This may need balance tuning post-launch.
- The cast overlay's existing `castHitZone` client variable must be replaced with server-provided bounds

RELATED EXISTING BEADS:
- harborheist-wqw.11 (TASK 14.11: Wire rod minigameZoneSize into client timing minigame) — partially overlaps; this epic subsumes it
- harborheist-fishing-system-rework-h2e.2 (TASK 3.2: Client timing minigame UI) — closed, but only the bite minigame was wired

title: TASK 16.2: Add CastResult server handler — compute accuracy tier, store luckBonus
description:
WHAT: Add a server-side handler for the CastResult RemoteEvent. It receives the client's reported marker position, re-derives the accuracy tier from the server-authoritative bounds (stored on activeBites by TASK 16.1), and stores the resulting luckBonus.

SECURITY: The server must NOT trust the client's claimed accuracy tier. It must re-compute the tier from the raw marker position against its own bounds. A client can lie about where the marker was, but the server clamps the resulting luckBonus to the config-defined maximums.

IMPLEMENTATION:
  remotes.CastResult.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player, accuracy)
    -- accuracy is the marker position [0,1] when the player clicked
    local biteData = activeBites[player]
    if not biteData or biteData.castResultReceived then return end
    biteData.castResultReceived = true
    -- Clamp accuracy to [0,1] (client could send out-of-range)
    accuracy = math.clamp(type(accuracy) == "number" and accuracy or 0, 0, 1)
    -- Derive tier from server-authoritative bounds
    local tier
    if accuracy >= biteData.goodStart and accuracy <= biteData.goodEnd then
      tier = "perfect"
    elseif accuracy >= biteData.hitZoneStart and accuracy <= biteData.hitZoneEnd then
      tier = "good"
    else
      tier = "ok"
    end
    biteData.luckBonus = GameConfig.MiniGame.accuracyLuckBonus[tier] or 0
  end)

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:

- [ ] Handler validates activeBites exists and isn't already processed
- [ ] Marker position clamped to [0,1]
- [ ] Tier derived from server bounds (goodStart/End → perfect, hitZoneStart/End → good, else ok)
- [ ] luckBonus set from GameConfig.MiniGame.accuracyLuckBonus[tier]
- [ ] Client cannot inflate luckBonus by sending a crafted accuracy value

title: EPIC 17: Dock Upgrade Tree Feature
description:
BACKGROUND: The DockUpgradeTiers config table (GameConfig.lua:105-110) defines 4 tiers with incomeMultiplier (1.0 → 1.6) and cosmetic unlocks (LampPost, Planters, GoldenTrim). This config has existed since the initial PRD-compliance implementation but was NEVER WIRED — there's no purchase path, no income-multiplier consumption, no cosmetic rendering, and no UI.

The round-2 review (EPIC 15) flagged this as checklist item #15 (Advertised Multiplier Never Applied). The user directed: "wire as feature."

DESIGN: Dock upgrades are an INCOME MULTIPLIER progression path, distinct from Aquarium upgrades (which add capacity + a smaller income multiplier). This gives players two parallel investment tracks:
  - Aquarium upgrades: more fish capacity + moderate income multiplier (1.0-1.5)
  - Dock upgrades: NO capacity change, but a LARGER income multiplier (1.0-1.6) + cosmetic flair

This creates a meaningful choice: do you spend 8000 on a Mega Tank (more fish, 1.5x) or 10000 on a Golden Trim dock (same fish, 1.6x + cosmetics)? The answer depends on playstyle — hoarders want capacity, min-maxers want the higher multiplier.

PRD ALIGNMENT:
  - TASK 2.6 (closed) defined the tier structure
  - TASK 6.4 (open) covers the purchase flow — this epic IMPLEMENTS it
  - The cosmetic unlocks (LampPost, Planters, GoldenTrim) are per-tier visual rewards

WHY THIS MATTERS: The income loop (store fish → earn passive income → buy upgrades → store more fish) is the core retention loop. Adding a second upgrade track doubles the progression depth without adding new mechanics — it's pure economy expansion using existing systems.

CONSIDERATIONS:
- DockUpgradeTiers is 1-indexed (level 1 = base, free). Purchases start at level 2.
- The income multiplier STACKS with the Aquarium multiplier (both apply in incomePerSec). A maxed player (Aquarium 4 + Dock 4) gets 1.5 * 1.6 = 2.4x base income per fish.
- Cosmetic unlocks need visual implementation (lamp posts, planters, gold trim on the dock model). This is scoped as a separate task (TASK 17.5) and can be deferred post-launch if needed.
- The profile already has `Dock = { UpgradeLevel = 1, CosmeticUnlocks = {} }` — the schema is ready.

- harborheist-game-content-definitions-pmr.6 (TASK 2.6: Dock upgrade tiers) — closed, defined the config

title: TASK 17.6: Clamp Dock.UpgradeLevel in sanitize() against DockUpgradeTiers
description:
WHAT: The sanitize() function currently accepts Dock.UpgradeLevel if it's >= 1, but doesn't clamp it against the DockUpgradeTiers table length. A crafted save with UpgradeLevel = 999 would be loaded and honored, causing DockUpgradeTiers[999] lookups to return nil downstream.

This is checklist item #10 (Persisted Capacity Trusted Without Tier Cross-Check) applied to the Dock track. The same fix pattern used for Aquarium.UpgradeLevel (N6 in DataManager) should be applied here.

IMPLEMENTATION (in the Dock branch of sanitize):
  if type(data.Dock.UpgradeLevel) == "number" and data.Dock.UpgradeLevel >= 1 then
    clean.Dock.UpgradeLevel = math.floor(data.Dock.UpgradeLevel)
  end
  -- Clamp against authoritative tier table (mirrors the Aquarium N6 pattern):
  local DockUpgradeTiers = GameConfig.DockUpgradeTiers
  local dockLevel = clean.Dock.UpgradeLevel or 1
  if DockUpgradeTiers and #DockUpgradeTiers > 0 then
    dockLevel = math.max(1, math.min(dockLevel, #DockUpgradeTiers))
    clean.Dock.UpgradeLevel = dockLevel
  end

title: DEC-1: Passive income scope (online-only vs capped offline)
description:
PRD Open Decision #1. AQUA-04 says 'accrues only while in-game for V1' but the income model section implies elapsed-time calculation with a cap — tension.

RECOMMENDATION: V1 online-only accrual with a claimable income pool (don't auto-add to cash), capped to prevent extreme accumulation. Offline earnings deferred to V1.1.

UX RISK (important): Switching from auto-income to claimable income is a significant behavior change. Players used to cash ticking up passively may feel 'punished' if they forget to claim. Mitigation: make CLAIM button prominent, auto-claim on logout save, show a glowing '+$X ready to claim' indicator. If playtesting shows confusion, consider a hybrid: small auto-claim threshold + manual claim for the rest.

BLOCKS: Epic 5 income model + DataStore key versioning (1.6). PRD refs: AQUA-04, AQUA-05.
notes: DECISION: V1 online-only accrual + claimable pool. UnclaimedIncome accumulates while player is online, capped at MAX_UNCLAIMED. Player must CLAIM via button. Auto-claim on logout save. Does NOT persist on load (resets to 0). Offline earnings deferred to V1.1. Rationale: simplest exploit-resistant model that still creates the claim interaction the PRD wants (AQUA-05).

title: EPIC R1: Deep-Review Data Integrity & Persistence Hardening
description:
EPIC R1 — umbrella for the data-persistence findings from CoralBays full-codebase deep review (2026-07-22, commissioned by the project owner).

PROVENANCE / METHOD
A fresh-eyes, line-by-line review of src/server/DataManager.lua (650 lines), src/shared/PlayerProfile.lua, and the onPlayerAdded/onPlayerRemoving handlers in src/server/init.server.lua, plus a cross-check of every profile.X write in all server services against the sanitize() whitelist. The review ran AFTER wqw.20 (non-blocking leave save), aa3af75 (analytics rejoin race), thj.2 (checkpoint saves), and TASK 10.5 (DataStore health) landed, so every finding here is residual — it survived those hardening passes.

WHY THIS MATTERS (project context)
Harbor Heist is server-authoritative: the DataStore profile is the ONLY durable truth for coins, equipment, stored fish, locks, and raid state. Every hour of player progression funnels through DataManager.save(). Persistence bugs are therefore the highest-blast-radius bug class in the project: they silently destroy player trust (lost fish/coins) and cannot be detected by clients. Several findings are narrow-window races rather than certain failures, but the windows widen exactly when the game is under stress (retry backoff during DataStore outages), which is when data loss hurts most.

SCOPE (children)
- A.1 Rejoin stale-MERGE overwrite (P1 bug) — complements existing xsk (stale-LOAD). Both share one root cause family: no per-UserId save ordering / last-write-wins discipline. Fixing A.1 and xsk TOGETHER with a per-UserId write token is recommended; see A.1 description for the unified design.
- A.2 clampCoins NaN passthrough (P1 bug)
- A.3 Timer rehydration bounds (P1 bug)
- A.4 Defense schema normalization (P2)
- A.5 DataStore health state machine dead wiring (P2)
- A.6 Autosave spawn efficiency (P3)
- A.7 Migration RNG seeding fairness (P3)

EXPLICITLY OUT OF SCOPE (already tracked elsewhere)
- RaidProtectionUntilTimestamp WRITE path: field is sanitized + read (9mu.5 gate, isEligibleRaidTarget) but nothing writes it yet. That is PLANNED work under harborheist-raid-defense-system-gdj.7 (defender immunity, PVP-06). Do not duplicate; gdj.7 implementer should note two consumers already exist.
- Rejoin stale-LOAD window: harborheist-xsk (FoggyTower, P2). Linked as related from A.1.

DONE WHEN: all children closed, DataStore writes provably cannot regress a fresher session, and the sanitize/clamp layer is total (no NaN/inf/skewed-timer path survives a round-trip).

title: R1.1: Rejoin stale-MERGE overwrite — deferred leave-save can clobber a fresher rejoined session
description:
SEVERITY: P1 (silent, permanent loss of NEW-session progress; narrow but real window that widens under DataStore stress).

FOUND BY: CoralBay deep review 2026-07-22 (data persistence domain). Complements harborheist-xsk (stale-LOAD direction, FoggyTower). This bead is the stale-MERGE direction.

ROOT CAUSE (first principles)
onPlayerRemoving (src/server/init.server.lua ~line 236) defers the leave-save via task.spawn(function() pcall(DataManager.save, player) DataManager.remove(player) end). DataManager.save issues UpdateAsync(key, mergeFn). UpdateAsync mergeFn (DataManager.lua ~lines 520-543) UNCONDITIONALLY assigns the captured profile table over whatever the store currently holds:
  existing.Coins = clampCoins(profile.Coins)
  existing.Equipment = profile.Equipment
  existing.Aquarium = profile.Aquarium
  ... (full-field replacement, not a field-wise max/merge)
The closure captures the OLD session profile. Sessions are keyed by Player OBJECT, so a same-UserId rejoin creates a NEW session under a NEW key — the old save never knows it exists.

FAILURE SCENARIO
1. Player leaves at T1; deferred save spawns (retries can stretch it to ~3.75s+ under failure).
2. Same UserId rejoins at T2 (new Player object); DataManager.load reads the key and gets the PRE-T1 data (that half is xsk).
3. New session plays: catches fish, sells, buys — checkpoint saves (thj.2) write FRESH data at T3.
4. Old deferred save lands at T4. Its mergeFn reads existing (=T3 fresh) but overwrites EVERY field with the stale T1 profile.
5. Result: everything earned in the new session between T2 and T4 is silently wiped. The player sees a rollback with no error anywhere.

WHY wqw.20 / aa3af75 DID NOT FIX THIS
aa3af75 closed the ANALYTICS half (UserId-keyed clearSession could wipe a rejoined players analytics). The merge race is the DATA half and is untouched — the spawned save still runs with no freshness check.

FIX RECIPE (unified with xsk — recommended single design)
Introduce per-UserId write ordering / last-write-wins discipline:
1. Track a monotonically increasing per-UserId writeToken (or use profile.LastSaveEpoch written by every save).
2. In the UpdateAsync mergeFn, compare existing.LastSaveEpoch against the session snapshot epoch; if existing is NEWER, abort the write (return nil from mergeFn to cancel the UpdateAsync).
3. Belt-and-braces: in onPlayerRemoving spawn, re-check before saving that no live session exists for the same UserId (scan Players for UserId match with a different Player object); if one exists, skip save entirely — the live session is authoritative and will checkpoint itself.
Option (3) alone fixes this bead; option (2) also hardens xsk and cross-server cases (TeleportService rejoins). Doing both is the recommended complete fix.

CONSIDERATIONS
- UpdateAsync mergeFn returning nil cancels the write WITHOUT consuming budget — use that, not a pre-check GetAsync (TOCTOU).
- Epoch seconds granularity is enough; two saves inside the same second with identical tokens should prefer the LIVE session (tie-break: live wins).
- Do NOT key sessions by UserId instead of Player object to fix this — that reintroduces the rejoin-join collision aa3af75 documented.
- BindToClose path (isShutdown) needs the same guard only if a rejoin can happen during shutdown; in practice shutdown kills the server so the old save is the last writer — leave BindToClose as-is and document why.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- [ ] A scripted Studio test (or reasoned trace comment) shows the T1->T4 scenario above no longer overwrites T3 data.
- [ ] UpdateAsync mergeFn aborts on stale token without erroring.
- [ ] No change to the normal leave/save/autosave happy paths (rojo build passes; existing checkpoint saves still fire).
- [ ] Comment in code links this bead and xsk so the next reviewer sees the whole race family.

title: R1.2: clampCoins passes NaN through — NaN coins reach DataStore, leaderstats, and purchase gates
description:
SEVERITY: P1 (data corruption that breaks UI and silently disables spending; survives save/load round-trips).

FOUND BY: CoralBay deep review 2026-07-22.

ROOT CAUSE
PlayerProfile.clampCoins (src/shared/PlayerProfile.lua ~lines 109-114):
  if type(value) ~= "number" then return 0 end
  return math.floor(math.max(0, math.min(MAX_COINS, value)))
NaN is a number in Lua, so it passes the type guard. Every subsequent operation propagates it: math.min(NaN, x)=NaN, math.max(0, NaN)=NaN, math.floor(NaN)=NaN. The function returns NaN.
Clamp is the LAST line of defense before Coins hits (a) the DataStore (UpdateAsync merge at DataManager.lua ~line 526), (b) IntValue leaderstats (StateSync.setupLeaderstats), (c) every purchase comparison (ShopService: profile.Coins < cost).

BLAST RADIUS
- leaderstats: IntValue.Value = NaN renders broken cash on the name tag.
- Purchases: (NaN < cost) is always false, so a NaN-coined player can BUY EVERYTHING for free — the deduction Coins = clampCoins(NaN - cost) stays NaN. This is an economy-destroying exploit IF a NaN ever enters the profile.
- Entry paths: corrupted legacy v1 data, a hostile or buggy intermediate write, arithmetic on nil coerced elsewhere (0/0), or inf-inf from a huge TotalCoinsEarned edge. None of these are likely TODAY, but the clamp exists precisely to be the total barrier — and it has a hole.
- DataStore JSON encoders typically reject or null NaN, producing save failures that look like flaky DataStore errors and trip the TASK 10.5 health tracker for the wrong reason.

FIX RECIPE
Add the canonical NaN test (NaN ~= NaN) and infinity clamp:
  function PlayerProfile.clampCoins(value)
      if type(value) ~= "number" or value ~= value then return 0 end
      if value == math.huge then return PlayerProfile.MAX_COINS end
      if value == -math.huge then return 0 end
      return math.floor(math.max(0, math.min(PlayerProfile.MAX_COINS, value)))
  end
One function, total barrier. Every caller (save merge, BuyItem, SellAll, SellFish, ClaimIncome) inherits the fix for free — that is why the fix belongs HERE and not at call sites.

CONSIDERATIONS
- value ~= value is the idiomatic IEEE-754 NaN check; do not use tostring comparisons.
- Also audit TotalCoinsEarned writes: they bypass clampCoins by design (stat counter), but a NaN there poisons analytics. Optional: same guard in sanitize for TotalCoinsEarned (return 0 on NaN).
- UBS cannot catch this (Lua unsupported); verification is by unit-style reasoning + rojo build.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- [ ] clampCoins(0/0) == 0; clampCoins(math.huge) == MAX_COINS; clampCoins(-math.huge) == 0.
- [ ] All existing clampCoins call sites unchanged and still correct.
- [ ] rojo build passes.

title: R1.3: Lock/cooldown timer rehydration has no sanity bounds — skewed epochs produce instant-expiry or multi-year locks
description:
SEVERITY: P1 (defense mechanic silently broken by corrupted or clock-skewed data; a permanently-stuck lock disables the owners own aquarium, an instantly-expiring lock strips paid-for protection).

FOUND BY: CoralBay deep review 2026-07-22.

ROOT CAUSE
DataManager.load (src/server/DataManager.lua ~lines 453-458) rehydrates persisted epoch timestamps into os.clock() deadlines:
  if profile.Aquarium.LockUntilTimestamp > nowEpoch then
      session.lockedUntil = os.clock() + (profile.Aquarium.LockUntilTimestamp - nowEpoch)
  end
The > nowEpoch guard only excludes FULLY expired timestamps. Two bad shapes survive:
1. FAR-FUTURE: timestamp = now + 6 years (data corruption, a buggy write, or a server whose clock was wrong at save time) -> lock lasts 6 years of os.clock time. The aquarium is bricked: SellAll blocked (wqw.6), 9mu.5 stored-fish sells blocked, raids blocked. Owner cannot unlock by design.
2. Same pattern for LockCooldownUntilTimestamp: cooldown becomes effectively permanent, so the Lock feature dies for that player.
(The past case is safe: <= nowEpoch skips rehydration. The danger is only unbounded future drift.)

WHY THIS IS A REAL RISK
Epoch timestamps cross process restarts and machine boundaries. Studio test servers, local clock edits, and any future write bug all feed this path. The rehydration layer is the trust boundary and currently trusts blindly.

FIX RECIPE
Clamp rehydrated durations to the design envelope (GameConfig.Aquarium lock duration/cooldown, currently <= 150s + 120s; use a generous ceiling like 1 hour to leave headroom for future upgrades):
  local MAX_REHYDRATE_SECONDS = 3600
  local function rehydrate(ts)
      local remaining = ts - os.time()
      if remaining <= 0 then return 0 end
      return os.clock() + math.min(remaining, MAX_REHYDRATE_SECONDS)
  end
Apply to BOTH LockUntilTimestamp and LockCooldownUntilTimestamp. Log a warn() when clamping fires so the corruption is visible in analytics-friendly output.

CONSIDERATIONS
- Derive the ceiling from GameConfig (max lockDuration + max lockCooldown across upgrade tiers) rather than a magic 3600, so balance changes cannot silently invalidate the bound. A small helper in GameConfig keeps this self-maintaining.
- Persisted epoch writes (DataManager.save ~lines 511-518) are symmetric: consider asserting there too that we never WRITE a timestamp more than ceiling into the future — catches the producer bug at the source.
- Same class of bug applies to any FUTURE persisted epoch (e.g. RaidProtectionUntilTimestamp once gdj.7 writes it): make the helper reusable now so gdj.7 inherits the protection.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- [ ] A profile with LockUntilTimestamp = os.time() + 10^7 loads with lockedUntil clamped to the ceiling, and a warn fires.
- [ ] Normal locks (60-150s) rehydrate unchanged across a server restart.
- [ ] Both timestamps use the shared helper; gdj.7 implementer is pointed at it via code comment.

title: R1.4: Defense profile table is created ad-hoc inside LockAquarium — normalize schema ownership into PlayerProfile.default/sanitize
description:
SEVERITY: P2 (no data loss today; schema drift and duplicated defaults that will bite the next Defense consumer).

FOUND BY: CoralBay deep review 2026-07-22.

ROOT CAUSE
AquariumService.LockAquarium (src/server/AquariumService.lua ~lines 232-235) defensively creates the Defense table inline when missing:
  local defense = session.profile.Defense
  if not defense then
      defense = { LockFreeUsesRemaining = 3, LockFreeUsesMax = 3 }
      session.profile.Defense = defense
  end
But PlayerProfile.default() already creates Defense with the same fields, and sanitize() (DataManager.lua ~lines 312-319) already reconstructs it on load. So this inline branch is (a) unreachable on any sanitized session, (b) a THIRD copy of the default values (3 free uses), (c) a place future edits will forget.

WHY IT MATTERS (first principles)
Schema must have ONE owner. Today the Defense shape lives in three places: PlayerProfile.default (canonical), DataManager.sanitize (repair), and this handler (ad-hoc). When gdj.x adds Defense.AlarmCharges or changes free-use counts, someone will update one or two copies and ship a silent inconsistency where a player who never triggers the ad-hoc path has a different Defense shape than one who does.

FIX RECIPE
1. Delete the inline creation from LockAquarium; index session.profile.Defense directly (sanitize guarantees it — that guarantee is the contract, and this handler may rely on it).
2. Add one assert-style guard with a clear message for the impossible case, so a future sanitize regression fails loudly at dev time instead of silently:
   local defense = session.profile.Defense
   assert(defense, "Defense missing: sanitize contract broken")
3. While here: hoist the magic numbers 3/3 into GameConfig.Defense = { LockFreeUsesMax = 3 } and have PlayerProfile.default read from it — single tuning home, consistent with how every other balance number lives in GameConfig.

CONSIDERATIONS
- The assert must be dev-only semantics: on live servers a missing Defense indicates corrupt sanitize input, and crashing the handler is worse than repairing. Prefer: if not defense then rebuild + warn (keeps availability) — the KEY change is single-sourcing the shape, not the failure mode. Choose warn-and-repair over assert for production empathy; note the tradeoff in the commit message.
- Check sanitize() writes Defense defaults from GameConfig too (same single-source goal) — that may require threading config access into sanitize; if that couples layers badly, leave sanitize literals and add a comment cross-referencing GameConfig.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- [ ] LockAquarium contains no inline Defense construction.
- [ ] LockFreeUsesMax default lives in exactly one place (GameConfig or PlayerProfile.default).
- [ ] A player joining with a Defense-less legacy save still locks successfully (warn + repair path exercised).
- [ ] rojo build passes.

title: R1.5: DataStore health state machine is half-wired — recordSuccess/recordFailure/tryRecover are dead code, recovery never runs
description:
SEVERITY: P2 (reliability feature from TASK 10.5 works only by accident of the save() path; designed recovery never happens; dead public API invites misuse).

FOUND BY: CoralBay deep review 2026-07-22.

ROOT CAUSE
DataManager exposes recordSuccess(), recordFailure(), and tryRecover() (~lines 624-645) as the public health API, but NOTHING in the codebase calls them. The only health transitions live inline inside DataManager.save() (~lines 548-559). Consequences:
1. tryRecover() is never invoked, so once isDataStoreHealthy flips false after 3 consecutive failures, it stays false until a save happens to succeed — but services may gate behavior on isHealthy() and reduce save attempts, making spontaneous recovery LESS likely. The intended cooldown-based recovery path is dead.
2. Loads (GetAsync failures in DataManager.load) do NOT feed the failure counter — a server where loads fail but saves never run reports healthy. Health currently means "save health only", which is not what the API names promise.
3. Dead exported functions are a trap: the next agent will call recordFailure from some new path and double-count, because save() already counts inline.

FIX RECIPE (choose ONE coherent design; recommendation below)
Option A (recommended — minimal, honest): make save()/load() the sole owners of health transitions.
  - Delete recordSuccess/recordFailure from the public surface (or make them local helpers called by save AND load).
  - Feed load failures into the same counter (a failed GetAsync is as much a DataStore outage signal as a failed UpdateAsync).
  - Call tryRecover() from the autosave loop once per tick (cheap, single scheduler) so recovery is actually attempted after FAILURE_COOLDOWN.
Option B: keep the public API and route ALL transitions through it (save/load call recordSuccess/recordFailure instead of inline mutation). More churn, same outcome. Only worth it if external services will report failures — currently none do.

CONSIDERATIONS
- TASK 10.5s design intent (from its commit fe7680e) was: after N consecutive failures mark unhealthy -> clients show a warning -> cooldown -> attempt recovery. The client-facing half (snapshot health flag) IS wired; the recovery half is not. This bead completes the original intent rather than redesigning it.
- Distinguish consecutive-failure semantics across save+load: a successful load should reset the counter only if we believe read-success implies write-health; safer to reset only on successful WRITE, and count both failure kinds. Document the chosen semantics in a comment.
- isHealthy() is consumed by StateSync.snapshot (client warning) — verify the flag flaps are not spamming clients; consider hysteresis (require 2 consecutive successes to flip back healthy) as a cheap stability win while touching this code.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- [ ] No dead exported health functions: every exported fn has >= 1 real caller, or is removed.
- [ ] Load failures participate in the health counter (or an explicit code comment explains why they must not).
- [ ] tryRecover (or its replacement) is invoked from a scheduled path and can flip a server back to healthy after an outage.
- [ ] Behavior under a simulated outage is documented in the bead close reason.

title: R1.6: Autosave spawns saves for sessions that may already be gone — recheck sessions at task-execution time
description:
SEVERITY: P3 (no data loss; wasted tasks and misleading warn spam during mass-leave events like server shutdown or a raid exodus).

FOUND BY: CoralBay deep review 2026-07-22.

ROOT CAUSE
DataManager.startAutosave (~lines 570-590) snapshots the player list, then checks `if sessions[player]` BEFORE task.spawn. The spawned closure itself does not recheck. Sequence: autosave ticks -> snapshot includes Player A -> A leaves -> onPlayerRemoving deferred remove() clears sessions[A] -> spawned save runs, DataManager.save(A) finds session=nil and early-returns. Harmless today because save() nil-guards, but:
1. Every leaving player generates one useless spawned task per tick (up to 8 players per server x however many ticks overlap the leave window).
2. If save()s nil-guard is ever refactored away (it is one line), the safety silently disappears — the invariant lives in the wrong place.
3. The early-return also SKIPS the isSaving wait loop, which is fine, but the pattern trains readers to believe spawned saves always operate on live sessions — that assumption breaks elsewhere (see R1.1 rejoin analysis).

FIX RECIPE
Move the liveness check INSIDE the spawned closure (execution time, not snapshot time):
  for _, player in ipairs(players) do
      task.spawn(function()
          if sessions[player] then
              DataManager.save(player)
          end
      end)
  end
Also drop the now-redundant pre-spawn check, keeping the snapshot of keys (which is still required to avoid pairs() mutation-during-iteration — that part of the existing design is correct and must stay).

CONSIDERATIONS
- This is a robustness/invariant-placement fix, not a perf fire. Do not gold-plate: no coroutine pooling, no batching changes.
- Keep the comment explaining WHY the snapshot-then-spawn shape exists (join-during-iteration safety) and extend it with WHY the recheck lives inside the closure (leave-during-dispatch safety). Future refactors need both halves of the story.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- [ ] Spawned autosave tasks verify session liveness at execution time.
- [ ] No behavioral change on the happy path (all live sessions still saved every 60s).
- [ ] Comment documents both race directions.

title: R1.7: v1->v2 migration species pick uses unseeded math.random — fairness + auditability of legacy fish conversion
description:
SEVERITY: P3 (theoretical fairness issue, no data loss; migration runs once per legacy player, but the conversion is permanent and un-auditable today).

FOUND BY: CoralBay deep review 2026-07-22.

ROOT CAUSE
FishInstance.fromRarityIndex (src/shared/FishInstance.lua ~lines 84-95, landed in wqw.12) picks the replacement species for a legacy v1 rarity-index fish via pool[math.random(1, #pool)] using the global math.random stream. Two issues:
1. FAIRNESS: the global stream is shared with every other math.random call on the server. The outcome for a given legacy player depends on how many unrelated rolls happened first — not on anything about that player. Two players with identical v1 liveWells can receive wildly different-value species of the same rarity (e.g. two Uncommons with different BaseSellValue), with no design intent behind the variance.
2. AUDITABILITY: the migration print log (DataManager.load ~line 405) records the SOURCE (cash/rodLevel/liveWell counts) but not the RESULT species list. If a legacy player disputes their converted aquarium, there is no way to reconstruct what they were given.

FIX RECIPE
1. Use a dedicated Random.new() instance seeded per-player (e.g. Random.new(userId + migrationEpoch)) so conversion outcomes are a deterministic-ish function of the player, not of global RNG history. (Full determinism is optional; isolation from the global stream is the point.)
2. Extend the migration log line to include the resulting species list: MIGRATION v1->v2: user=X source{...} result{Bluegill x2, Carp x1}. One extra string.format, permanent auditability.

CONSIDERATIONS
- Do NOT seed the global math.random anywhere on the server — that would couple unrelated systems (fishing rolls use Random.new() instances already, keep it that way).
- Seeding with os.time() alone reintroduces predictability across servers booting in the same second; userId in the seed breaks that symmetry.
- This only affects the ONE-TIME migration path; runtime fish creation already goes through proper Random instances (verified in the fishing-domain review, invariant #6).

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- [ ] Migration species selection uses a per-player Random instance, not global math.random.
- [ ] Migration log records the resulting species list.
- [ ] A v1 fixture profile migrates to the same species set given the same seed inputs (documented in close reason).

title: EPIC R2: Deep-Review Economy Unification & Config Validation
description:
EPIC R2 — umbrella for the fishing/economy findings from CoralBays full-codebase deep review (2026-07-22).

PROVENANCE / METHOD
Line-by-line review of src/server/FishingService.lua, src/shared/GameConfig.lua, FishDefinitions.lua, FishInstance.lua, ZoneDefinitions.lua, and RodService.lua AFTER wqw.4 (bite window 3.5s) and wqw.24 (cast luckBonus inflates effective bite zone to ceiling 0.85) landed. The review VERIFIED 11 core invariants correct (zone nesting, server-authoritative accuracy tiers, re-roll 15% hard floor, luck stacking, cleanup on leave, os.clock/os.time discipline, protocol desync guards). The findings below are the residual issues.

WHY THIS MATTERS (project context)
The economy is the retention engine: stored fish generate passive income, income buys upgrades, upgrades catch rarer fish. If the three income definitions (GameConfig.Rarities[].incomePerSec, FishDefinitions.Species[].IncomePerMinute, Economy.IncomeToValueRatio) disagree — and they currently disagree by up to 16x on the same fish — then every tuning pass lies to someone: either the shop UI, the audit log, or the actual accrual. Silent divergence is worse than a wrong number. Separately, the wqw.24 ceiling math is correct TODAY but only because the config happens to satisfy two unenforced inequalities (ceiling > every rod zone size; perfect zone nested in good zone). A future balance edit can silently invert the skill incentive.

SCOPE (children)
- B.1 Income-field consumption audit (P1) — read-only inventory of which definition is actually live.
- B.2 Unify income to a single source of truth (P1, blocked by B.1).
- B.3 Startup income invariant assertion (P2, blocked by B.2).
- B.4 Startup config-validation harness (P2) with subtasks B.4.1 (ceiling vs rod zones), B.4.2 (perfect subset of good), B.4.3 (rarity-order monotonicity).
- B.5 Dynamic RARITY_ORDER derivation (P3).

DESIGN INTENT (for future self)
The review recommendation is BaseSellValue x IncomeToValueRatio as the single source (PRD V1 passive-income model: income derived from value, capped by MaxUnclaimedIncome). But B.1 must confirm what is actually consumed before B.2 deletes anything — GameConfig.Rarities[].incomePerSec may be dead config, or may have a consumer outside the reviewed files (e.g. docs, shop UI strings). Verify, then cut.

DONE WHEN: exactly one function computes income-per-time for a fish, every config invariant that the minigame math assumes is asserted at server boot, and deleting a rarity from GameConfig cannot silently desync FishDefinitions.

title: R2.1: Audit which of the three income definitions is actually live (consumption inventory)
description:
TYPE: read-only investigation + written report (no code changes). Blocks R2.2.

FOUND BY: CoralBay deep review 2026-07-22 (fishing domain, finding HIGH-1).

BACKGROUND — THE THREE DEFINITIONS
Income-per-time for a stored fish is currently DEFINED in three places that disagree by up to 16x on the same fish:
1. GameConfig.Rarities[].incomePerSec (src/shared/GameConfig.lua ~lines 8-12): Common=0.2/sec => 12/min.
2. FishDefinitions.Species[].IncomePerMinute (src/shared/FishDefinitions.lua): e.g. Bluegill (Common) = 1/min. Consumed by FishInstance.new -> fish.IncomePerMinute -> StateSync.incomePerSec (the LIVE accrual path, verified: AquariumService income loop reads stateSync.incomePerSec).
3. GameConfig.Economy.IncomeToValueRatio (0.05): implies BaseSellValue x 0.05 => Bluegill(15) = 0.75/min.

The LIVE path today is #2 (FishInstance.IncomePerMinute, summed in StateSync.incomePerSec with tier multipliers). #1 and #3 are suspected dead-or-misleading config, but this was only verified for the reviewed files — a consumer may exist in shop UI strings, client display code (init.client.lua income previews), docs, or analytics.

WHY AUDIT BEFORE CUTTING (first principles)
Deleting config that a UI label reads produces silent wrong-tooltips (the worst kind: players make decisions on false numbers). Keeping dead config that looks authoritative guarantees the next balance pass edits the wrong table. The only safe move is an exhaustive consumer inventory first.

SCOPE OF AUDIT
- rg for: incomePerSec, IncomePerMinute, IncomeToValueRatio, incomePerMinute across ALL of src/ (server, client, shared), docs/, PRD.md, scripts/.
- For each hit classify: LIVE (affects accrual), DISPLAY (affects UI text), DOC (documentation), DEAD (no consumer).
- Special attention: src/client/init.client.lua (income preview labels), ShopService/shop UI (does any upgrade description quote income numbers derived from a different definition?), StateSync.snapshot fields sent to client.

DELIVERABLE
A comment on this bead (or short docs note) listing every reference with its classification, plus the recommended single source of truth for R2.2. Recommendation going in: keep #2 (FishInstance carries IncomePerMinute, because per-species variation is a design feature — a tank of Commons should differ by species), DERIVE it from BaseSellValue x IncomeToValueRatio at FishInstance.new time (kills the hand-maintained duplication), and DELETE Rarities[].incomePerSec. But the audit may reveal constraints that flip this.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- [ ] Every textual reference to the three fields is classified LIVE/DISPLAY/DOC/DEAD.
- [ ] The chosen single source is justified against PRD V1 passive-income model (income derived from value, capped by MaxUnclaimedIncome).
- [ ] R2.2 can start with zero open questions.

title: R2.2: Unify fish income to a single source of truth (kill the 16x divergence)
description:
SEVERITY: P1 (economy correctness: tuning edits made against the wrong table silently do nothing — or worse, the UI quotes rates the accrual never pays).

Blocked by R2.1 (audit must complete first). FOUND BY: CoralBay deep review 2026-07-22 (HIGH-1).

GOAL
Exactly ONE function/field computes income-per-time for a fish. Everything else derives from it or is deleted.

EXPECTED SHAPE (subject to R2.1 findings)
1. FishInstance.new computes IncomePerMinute = BaseSellValue x GameConfig.Economy.IncomeToValueRatio (rounded sensibly, min 0 or a documented floor) unless FishDefinitions overrides it per-species for deliberate design variance (document the override as the exception path).
2. Delete GameConfig.Rarities[].incomePerSec (or, if the audit finds a live consumer, convert that consumer to the unified value first, then delete).
3. Any DISPLAY consumer (shop/income UI) reads the same computed value the accrual uses — no parallel math client-side. If the client needs it, StateSync.snapshot must send it (check snapshot first; it may already send incomePerSec).
4. Migration: existing stored FishInstance records persist IncomePerMinute. Decide + document: (a) leave legacy values (players keep grandfathered rates — simpler, kindest), or (b) recompute on load in sanitize (consistency, but silently nerfs/buffs existing players). Default to (a) with a code comment; (b) only with a migration log line.

CONSIDERATIONS
- MaxUnclaimedIncome cap (GameConfig.Economy, 50000) and tier multipliers (N13 aquarium, N17 dock) are DOWNSTREAM of the per-fish value and unaffected — do not touch them here.
- Balance impact: switching Bluegill from hardcoded 1/min to 15x0.05=0.75/min is a nerf to Commons; the audit table from R2.1 should include the before/after per-species delta so the balance owner can adjust IncomeToValueRatio in the same PR if they want parity. THAT DECISION BELONGS TO THE BALANCE OWNER — this bead unifies the plumbing and surfaces the numbers; it does not pick the economy level.
- Keep FishInstance.validate in sync if IncomePerMinute becomes derived (it may currently require the field to exist; derived-at-construction keeps it present, so likely no change).

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- [ ] One definition site; all consumers use it (accrual == display == audit log).
- [ ] Dead fields removed or explicitly marked deprecated with a removal bead.
- [ ] Legacy-player decision implemented + documented.
- [ ] Before/after per-species income table attached to the bead close reason for the balance owner.
- [ ] rojo build passes; income loop math unchanged for unaffected species.

title: R2.3: Startup assertion — income invariant (accrual path can never disagree with the canonical definition again)
description:
SEVERITY: P2 (regression fence for R2.2; prevents silent re-divergence).

Blocked by R2.2. FOUND BY: CoralBay deep review 2026-07-22.

INTENT
R2.2 fixes the divergence once. This bead makes it IMPOSSIBLE TO REINTRODUCE: a server-boot self-check that fails loudly (warn/error in Studio, non-fatal in production) if the invariant breaks.

WHAT TO ASSERT (finalize per R2.2 outcome)
For every species in FishDefinitions: computed IncomePerMinute == canonical formula result (within rounding tolerance). If R2.2 keeps per-species overrides, assert instead: every override is whitelisted in an explicit OVERRIDES table with a comment justifying it (no stealth hand-tuning).
Also assert GameConfig.Economy.IncomeToValueRatio is in a sane band (0 < ratio <= 0.5) — a typo like 5.0 would 100x the economy overnight.

CONSIDERATIONS
- Boot-time, not runtime: run once in init.server.lua after services load (or in a GameConfig.validate() called first). Fail with a loud warn listing every violating species; do not hard-crash a production server (availability), DO hard-fail in Studio (fast feedback). Pattern: if RunService:IsStudio() then error(...) else warn(...) end.
- This pairs naturally with the R2.4 config-validation harness — implement as ONE GameConfig.validate() with named checks so R2.4.1-3 add their assertions to the same function. Coordinate the file reservation if both beads run concurrently (both touch GameConfig.lua or a new validate module).

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- [ ] Boot check exists, named, and runs on every server start.
- [ ] Introducing a deliberate divergence in a test branch produces the expected loud failure in Studio.
- [ ] No measurable boot cost (it is an O(#species) arithmetic loop).

title: R2.4: Startup config-validation harness — assert the inequalities the minigame math silently assumes
description:
SEVERITY: P2 (prevention: today the math is correct ONLY because config happens to satisfy unenforced constraints; a future balance edit can silently invert skill incentives).

FOUND BY: CoralBay deep review 2026-07-22 (findings MEDIUM-1, MEDIUM-2, LOW-3).

BACKGROUND — THE ASSUMED INVARIANTS
wqw.24 made the effective bite zone interpolate from the rod base zone up to GameConfig.MiniGame.biteZoneCeiling (0.85) driven by cast luckBonus, via math.clamp(effectiveZone, baseZone, ceiling) (FishingService.lua ~line 335). The clamp is only incentive-preserving when ceiling >= baseZone for EVERY rod. Separately, the accuracy-tier logic (~lines 232-245) classifies perfect-first, then good — correct only when the perfect zone is strictly nested inside the good zone (perfectSize <= goodZoneWidth, currently 0.30-0.40 vs 0.5). Both inequalities hold TODAY and are enforced by NOTHING. A balance pass that shrinks the ceiling below a rod zone size makes perfect casts REDUCE success rate; one that grows a rod zone past the good width misclassifies tiers. Both failures are SILENT (math.clamp and if/elseif do not complain).

DESIGN INTENT
One GameConfig.validate() (new function in GameConfig.lua or a small shared/ConfigValidate module), called once at server boot from init.server.lua, Studio-fatal / production-warn (same pattern as R2.3 — share the helper). Each check is a named assertion with a message that says WHAT broke and WHERE to fix it. Subtasks R2.4.1 / R2.4.2 / R2.4.3 define the three initial checks; future config invariants should be added here by convention (mention in the module header comment).

WHY A HARNESS INSTEAD OF THREE INLINE ASSERTS
Inline asserts rot next to code that changes; a named, boot-time validation entry point becomes the documented place where config contracts live, and gives CI/Studio a single failure surface. Cost: one file, one call. Benefit: every future balance edit is machine-checked.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- [ ] GameConfig.validate() (or equivalent) runs at boot; contains the three subtask checks, each with a descriptive failure message.
- [ ] Studio boot fails loudly on a deliberately broken config; production warns and continues.
- [ ] Module header documents the convention: new config invariants get added here.

title: R2.4.1: Assert biteZoneCeiling >= every rod minigameZoneSize
description:
Subtask of R2.4 (config-validation harness). FOUND BY: CoralBay deep review 2026-07-22 (MEDIUM-1).

INVARIANT: for every entry in GameConfig.RodDefinitions, minigameZoneSize <= GameConfig.MiniGame.biteZoneCeiling.

WHY: FishingService (~line 335) computes effectiveZone = clamp(baseZone + luck-scaled bonus, baseZone, ceiling). If ceiling < baseZone for any rod, the clamp returns ceiling for ALL luck levels on that rod: perfect casts give ZERO bonus (incentive inversion), and worse, the effective zone could drop BELOW the honest base zone — skilled play literally punished. Current values are safe (rods 0.30/0.35/0.40, ceiling 0.85); this check keeps them safe forever.

IMPLEMENTATION: in GameConfig.validate(), loop RodDefinitions, assert with message naming the rod level and both values, e.g. "config: rod 3 minigameZoneSize 0.90 exceeds biteZoneCeiling 0.85 — raise ceiling or shrink rod zone".

ACCEPTANCE: deliberate config break (ceiling=0.25) fails Studio boot with the named message; valid config passes.

title: R2.4.2: Assert perfect zone nested inside good zone for every rod
description:
Subtask of R2.4 (config-validation harness). FOUND BY: CoralBay deep review 2026-07-22 (MEDIUM-2).

INVARIANT: for every rod, minigameZoneSize <= GameConfig.MiniGame.goodZoneWidth (currently 0.5), AND goodZoneWidth < 1.0 (zones must fit inside [0,1] with the centering margins from FishingService ~line 113: center drawn from [halfGood, 1-halfGood]).

WHY: the tier classifier (~lines 232-245) checks perfect first, then good. Perfect-wider-than-good breaks the nesting assumption: the zone-center draw range (derived from halfGood) can push the wider perfect zone out of [0,1], and tier boundaries stop matching what the client renders (client receives perfect+good bounds via CastState and renders both; misnested zones = misleading UI + wrong luck bonuses). Current values safe (0.30-0.40 <= 0.5); keep them safe.

IMPLEMENTATION: two named asserts in GameConfig.validate(): (a) per-rod perfect<=good, (b) 0 < goodZoneWidth < 1. Messages name the rod/values. BONUS (cheap, same loop): assert zone-center draw interval is non-empty: halfGood <= 1 - halfGood, i.e. goodZoneWidth <= 1.

ACCEPTANCE: deliberate break (rod zone 0.6) fails Studio boot naming the rod; valid config passes.

title: R2.4.3: Assert rarity weight/order monotonicity across GameConfig.Rarities and FishDefinitions.RARITY_ORDER
description:
Subtask of R2.4 (config-validation harness). FOUND BY: CoralBay deep review 2026-07-22 (LOW-3).

INVARIANT: FishDefinitions.RARITY_ORDER (hardcoded map Common=1..Legendary=5, ~line 288) must agree with the ARRAY ORDER of GameConfig.Rarities, because two independent code paths scale luck by ordinal: GameConfig.rollRarity uses the array index i, FishDefinitions.getRandomInZone uses RARITY_ORDER[name]. Reordering Rarities (or renaming a rarity) without touching the hardcoded map silently desyncs species weighting from rarity rolling — e.g. luck starts buffing the WRONG bucket.

ALSO CHECK (same pass, cheap): rarity weights are non-increasing down the array (Common heaviest) — an inverted weight (Legendary weight > Common weight) would flip the economy and is exactly the kind of typo a balance edit produces.

IMPLEMENTATION: build the ordinal map FROM GameConfig.Rarities inside validate() and deep-compare to RARITY_ORDER; assert weights monotonic non-increasing. Messages name the mismatching rarity. NOTE: R2.5 (dynamic RARITY_ORDER) makes the first check obsolete-by-construction; if R2.5 lands first, implement only the weight-monotonicity half and close this bead noting the overlap.

ACCEPTANCE: swapping two entries in GameConfig.Rarities fails Studio boot naming the desynced rarity; weight inversion fails likewise; valid config passes.

title: R2.5: Derive FishDefinitions.RARITY_ORDER from GameConfig.Rarities (delete the hardcoded duplicate)
description:
SEVERITY: P3 (robustness; no live bug today). FOUND BY: CoralBay deep review 2026-07-22 (LOW-3).

ROOT CAUSE: FishDefinitions.lua (~line 288) hardcodes RARITY_ORDER = { Common=1, ..., Legendary=5 }, duplicating the array order of GameConfig.Rarities. Two consumers scale luck by ordinal and must agree (rollRarity uses array index; getRandomInZone uses the map). The duplication exists only because the map predates a derive-at-boot helper.

FIX: at module load in FishDefinitions, build the map by iterating GameConfig.Rarities (name -> index), replacing the literal. One small loop; zero runtime cost after boot; makes R2.4.3s desync check obsolete-by-construction (keep that beads weight-monotonicity half).

CONSIDERATIONS: FishDefinitions already requires GameConfig (verify import order — no circular require: GameConfig must not require FishDefinitions; check before implementing. If a cycle appears, export a small init function instead and call it from init.server.lua before services start). Update the module header comment to document the derivation.

ACCEPTANCE: RARITY_ORDER is computed, not literal; deleting/reordering a rarity in GameConfig propagates correctly; rojo build passes; coordinate with R2.4.3 owner to avoid double-implementing the desync check.

title: BUG 15.1 [FIXED]: DataManager nil-deref on first join (data.dailyQuestKey)
description:
SEVERITY: CRITICAL — 100% reproducible crash on EVERY new player's first join.

ROOT CAUSE: DataManager.load() (line 335) read `data.dailyQuestKey` from the raw saved-data parameter, but `data` is nil for brand-new players (no DataStore entry) or when the datastore load fails. Indexing nil throws "attempt to index nil with 'dailyQuestKey'", crashing the session initialization.

WHY IT WAS MISSED: The sanitize() call above it (`local profile = sanitize(saved)`) looks like it handles everything, so the later `data.dailyQuestKey` reads seem safe. But `data` is the original function parameter, not the sanitized output. This only crashes on first join or datastore failure — easy to miss in testing if you always have existing save data.

FIX APPLIED (N2): Read from `profile.dailyQuestKey` (the sanitized result, guaranteed non-nil) instead of `data.dailyQuestKey`.

This is a NEW bug class (#12 in the server-authority-gap-checklist): raw-parameter dereference in load functions. Added to the skill's permanent checklist.

title: BUG 15.3 [FIXED]: Quest rewards never credited — session.cash does not exist
description:
SEVERITY: CRITICAL — quest completion shows "+$X" toast but credits ZERO coins, AND errors silently ("arithmetic on nil value").

ROOT CAUSE: QuestService.processList (line 87) wrote `session.cash += q.reward`. The session object (DataManager.lua:311-339) has no `cash` field — money lives at `session.profile.Coins`. The `session.cash +=` operation creates a new transient field that is never read by anything and never persisted. Worse, `+=` on nil errors with "attempt to perform arithmetic on a nil value" inside the quest loop.

FIX APPLIED (N4): Replaced with:
  session.profile.Coins = PlayerProfile.clampCoins(session.profile.Coins + q.reward)
  session.profile.TotalCoinsEarned = session.profile.TotalCoinsEarned + q.reward

This routes through clampCoins (matching every other coin-grant path) and tracks lifetime earnings. Added `require(PlayerProfile)` import to QuestService.

IMPACT: Every daily and weekly quest (11 templates, 3 daily + 2 weekly slots) was silently broken. Players could see the completion notification but received no reward. The error happened inside a loop in a potentially task.spawn'd context, so it may have silently broken ALL quest progression (not just the completing quest).

title: BUG 15.9 [FIXED]: TOCTOU race in steal resolution — stale index could steal raid-protected fish
description:
SEVERITY: CRITICAL (latent) — raid-protected Legendary fish could be stolen despite IsRaidProtected check.

FOUND BY: Background audit subagent (C6 in its report). The parent pass missed this because the race window is currently safe (single-threaded Luau, no yields between eligibility check and table.remove). But the code is FRAGILE — any future refactor that adds a yield (task.spawn, remote call) between snapshot and remove would make it exploitable.

ROOT CAUSE: handleSteal builds an `eligible` list of INDICES (positions in victimFish) for non-raid-protected fish. After the rng roll picks `stolenIndex = eligible[N]`, `table.remove(victimFish, stolenIndex)` removes at that index. If the victim sold/stored a fish between the eligibility snapshot and the remove (via a concurrent SellAll or StoreSingleFish), the indices shift, and `table.remove(victimFish, 3)` could now point at a DIFFERENT fish — possibly a raid-protected Legendary.

FIX APPLIED (N15): Capture the fish REFERENCE (not index) at selection time. Re-find it in the live list via identity comparison (`fish == targetFish`), re-validate `not fish.IsRaidProtected`, then remove. If the target vanished or became protected, fail-safe as a miss rather than stealing the wrong fish.

title: TASK 14.11: Wire rod minigameZoneSize into client timing minigame
description:

title: TASK 14.16: Server-side validation of catch minigame hit (CRITICAL authority gap)
description:
EXPLOIT — the single largest server-authority hole in the codebase.

## ROOT CAUSE
The catch minigame's hit determination is CLIENT-SIDE: the client computes `hit = markerPos >= 0.35 and markerPos <= 0.65` (src/client/init.client.lua:496) and sends `{hit = <boolean>}` to the server. The server at src/server/FishingService.lua:135-145 only validates `type(timingResult.hit) == "boolean"` — it NEVER re-derives whether the hit was legitimate. An exploiter can fire:

    SubmitCatchInput:InvokeServer({hit = true})

...during any active bite window and ALWAYS catch the fish, regardless of where the marker actually was. The server clears activeBites[player] on first submit (line 140) so repeat submissions fail, but a single forged hit=true always succeeds.

## IMPACT
The entire skill-based timing minigame is a formality. Exploiters bypass it completely and catch every fish. This undermines the core gameplay loop and any economy balance built on catch rates.

## FIX RECIPE
The server cannot see the client's marker position (client-only state), so true server-side hit validation requires re-architecting the minigame protocol. Two options, in order of preference:

OPTION A (server-driven marker, RECOMMENDED): Server picks a random target window [t0, t1] within [0,1] at bite time, sends it to the client in BiteEvent. Client renders marker + target, reports only the marker position at tap time. Server checks `t0 <= markerPos <= t1`. This moves hit validation server-side without trusting the client's boolean.

OPTION B (plausibility check, quicker): Server validates that the reported markerPos is within the CURRENT rod's minigameZoneSize bounds (from GameConfig.Rods[rodLevel].minigameZoneSize, after TASK 14.10/14.11 wire it up). This catches the trivial always-hit-true exploit but not a smart exploiter who sends markerPos in the zone.

RECOMMENDED: Option A. It's a protocol change but eliminates the exploit class entirely.

## CONSIDERATIONS
- Depends on TASK 14.10 (rod consolidation) and 14.11 (minigameZoneSize wiring) for the zone-size data.
- The target zone is currently CENTERED at 0.5 with width 0.30. If we keep it centered, Option B is weaker (exploiter knows the zone). Option A with a RANDOM center is much stronger.
- Client must render the target zone at the server-specified position, not hardcoded center.

## FILES
src/server/FishingService.lua (BiteEvent payload + SubmitCatchInput validation), src/client/init.client.lua (render server-specified zone, report markerPos not hit boolean)
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Server picks target zone bounds at bite time and sends in BiteEvent
- [ ] Client renders zone from server data (not hardcoded)
- [ ] Client sends markerPos, not hit boolean
- [ ] Server validates markerPos is within the zone it chose
- [ ] Exploiter sending hit=true with markerPos outside zone is rejected
- [ ] UBS clean on FishingService.lua and init.client.lua

title: TASK 14.19: Wire luck stat into species roll (currently dead)
description:
Progression integrity — rods/bait should actually improve catch rarity.

## ROOT CAUSE
src/server/FishingService.lua:157 computes `local luck = rod.luck + bait.luck` and then NEVER USES IT. The species roll at line 158 calls `FishDefinitions.getRandomInZone(zoneId, rng)` which uses ONLY CatchWeight — no luck modifier. Meanwhile GameConfig.rollRarity(luck, rng) (src/shared/GameConfig.lua:90) exists and implements luck-weighted rarity rolling, but it's never called either. The result: buying a Steel Rod (+8 luck) or Magic Bait (+15 luck) changes NOTHING about what fish you catch. Only cast time (rod.castTime) has any effect.

## IMPACT
Core progression is a lie. Players spend 500-2500 coins on gear that does nothing for catch quality. The PRD's "upgrade -> catch better fish" loop is broken.

## FIX RECIPE
Modify FishDefinitions.getRandomInZone to accept an optional luck parameter and weight rarer species higher:

    function FishDefinitions.getRandomInZone(zoneId, rng, luck)
        luck = luck or 0
        local pool = FishDefinitions.ByZone[zoneId]
        if not pool or #pool == 0 then return nil end
        local total = 0
        local weights = {}
        for i, def in ipairs(pool) do
            -- Boost weight by luck, scaled by rarity tier (rarer = more boost)
            local rarityBoost = 1
            for ri, r in ipairs(GameConfig.Rarities) do
                if r.name == def.Rarity then
                    rarityBoost = 1 + (luck / 100) * (ri - 1)
                    break
                end
            end
            local w = def.CatchWeight * rarityBoost
            weights[i] = w
            total += w
        end
        local roll = (rng and rng:NextNumber() or math.random()) * total
        local acc = 0
        for i, def in ipairs(pool) do
            acc += weights[i]
            if roll <= acc then return def end
        end
        return pool[1]
    end

Then in FishingService.lua:158, pass the luck: `FishDefinitions.getRandomInZone(zoneId, rng, luck)`.

## CONSIDERATIONS
- The luck formula mirrors GameConfig.rollRarity's approach (weight *= (1 + luck/100 * (rarityIndex - 1))) for consistency.
- With max gear (Golden Rod +20, Magic Bait +15 = 35 luck), a Legendary's weight is boosted by 1 + 0.35 * 4 = 2.4x — noticeable but not game-breaking.
- FishDefinitions needs access to GameConfig for the rarity ordering; it currently doesn't require it. Add the require.
- This obsoletes GameConfig.rollRarity (which operates on the old 5-tier system, not species). Mark rollRarity as deprecated or remove it (with approval).

## FILES
src/shared/FishDefinitions.lua (getRandomInZone signature + weighting), src/server/FishingService.lua (pass luck), src/shared/GameConfig.lua (deprecate rollRarity)

title: TASK 14.20: Make onPlayerRemoving save non-blocking
description:
Reliability — prevent data loss on fast player exits.

## ROOT CAUSE
src/server/init.server.lua:104-114 (onPlayerRemoving) calls DataManager.save(player) SYNCHRONOUSLY. DataManager.save does UpdateAsync inside withRetries with up to 4 attempts and exponential backoff (~0.25 + 0.5 + 1.0 + 2.0 = ~3.75s worst case, plus the actual DataStore call time). Roblox's PlayerRemoving handler has a limited execution budget; on fast exits or server shutdown, this can be killed mid-save, silently losing the player's recent progress.

## IMPACT
Data loss on crash-y exits or when the leave handler budget is exceeded.

## FIX RECIPE
Two complementary fixes:

1. In DataManager.save, reduce max retries from 4 to 2 when called from a shutdown context (add an optional `isShutdown` param). On shutdown, a fast-failing save is better than a slow save that gets killed.

2. In init.server.lua onPlayerRemoving, wrap the save in task.spawn so the handler returns immediately:

    task.spawn(function()
        DataManager.save(player)
        DockManager.release(player)
        DataManager.remove(player)
    end)

   NOTE: Roblox's BindToClose gives ~30s, but PlayerRemoving does NOT block shutdown. Spawning means the save might not complete before the player object is fully destroyed — but DataManager.save only reads session data (already captured), so it's safe as long as sessions[player] isn't cleared first.

## CONSIDERATIONS
- Order matters: release dock and remove session AFTER save completes.
- If the server is shutting down (BindToClose), the save in bindToClose's loop is the authoritative one; onPlayerRemoving's save is best-effort.

## FILES
src/server/init.server.lua (spawn save), src/server/DataManager.lua (optional retry-count param)
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] onPlayerRemoving does not block on save
- [ ] Save still completes in normal (non-shutdown) exits
- [ ] BindToClose path unchanged
- [ ] UBS clean on init.server.lua and DataManager.lua
close_reason: Completed (both parts). Part 2 (mine, init.server.lua onPlayerRemoving): wrapped save + dependent cleanup in task.spawn so the PlayerRemoving handler returns immediately instead of blocking on a synchronous UpdateAsync (4 retries + backoff) that can be killed mid-write when the leave handler budget expires. Ordering preserved: fishingCleanup + EPIC-11 funnel churn events fire synchronously first (always run); inside the spawn, save -> release -> BoatService -> RodService -> clearSession -> remove, with remove() (clears sessions[player]) deferred until AFTER save completes since save reads sessions[player]. Part 1 (DataManager.lua, stranded WIP from a prior session, now landed): DataManager.save takes optional isShutdown -> withRetries uses 2 attempts on shutdown (4 otherwise); BindToClose calls save(player, true) since its 30s budget can't be escaped by spawning. onPlayerRemoving's spawned save keeps 4 retries (spawn frees it from the leave-handler budget). title: DESIGN 14.24: Honest-client catch rate — server-authority re-roll decouples minigame skill from outcome
description:
TYPE: DESIGN DECISION (not a bug) — needs a gameplay design call before implementation.

PROBLEM: The N16 anti-exploit re-roll in SubmitCatchInput (rng:NextNumber() > minigameZoneSize → miss, TASK 14.16) makes the boolean hit fully server-authoritative — but as a SIDE EFFECT, an honest player who perfectly times the minigame only succeeds zoneSize% of the time:
  - Basic Rod (zoneSize 0.30): ~30% catch rate on a PERFECT tap
  - Steel Rod (0.35): ~35%
  - Golden Rod (0.40): ~40%

So the bite minigame's skill is DECOUPLED from the outcome. The code comment claiming "honest clients are unaffected" is incorrect — honest clients who hit the zone still miss 60-70% of the time. This makes the timing minigame feel pointless and punishing.

SECURITY CONTEXT: The re-roll exists to close the boolean-trust exploit (client sends hit=true always). Any fix MUST preserve server authority on the final outcome — the client can never be trusted to declare hit/miss.

DESIGN SPACE (pick one or hybrid):
  A) Status quo (pure re-roll): secure but feel-bad; minigame is theater.
  B) Server-authoritative marker protocol: server picks zone bounds + marker trajectory seed, sends to client; client plays minigame against server-defined zones and reports raw input (tap timestamp + position); server re-derives hit from the same deterministic trajectory. Eliminates trust entirely while making skill REAL. Highest effort; the "right" long-term fix.
  C) Blended: keep re-roll as the base security floor, but let the new EPIC-16 cast-accuracy luckBonus + a bite-timing accuracy bonus shift the effective zone size up on good play (capped). E.g., a perfect bite tap could raise zoneSize toward a ceiling (~0.85). Preserves server authority, rewards skill, low effort — but the re-roll still randomly misses on some honest perfect taps.
  D) Remove the timing minigame from the hit decision entirely: hit is always granted server-side (bite = guaranteed hook), and the minigame ONLY determines rarity/quality (bigger luck bonus for better timing). Simplest and feel-good; bite becomes a reward-pacing UI rather than a skill gate. Changes difficulty meaningfully.

RECOMMENDATION: (C) as the pragmatic V1 fix (low effort, keeps security floor, restores skill expression), with (B) as the aspirational follow-up if timing-skill becomes a core differentiator. Document choice in this bead when decided.

WHY THIS MATTERS: The fishing loop is the core engagement loop. If the skill check is theater, players disengage. This is the single most impactful feel decision in the game right now.

RELATED: TASK 14.16 (closed — introduced the re-roll), EPIC 16 (closed — wired cast accuracy as a luck bonus), GameConfig.MiniGame.accuracyLuckBonus.
close_reason: DECISION C implemented (server-only, server-authority preserved). The server-authoritative cast-accuracy luckBonus (re-derived in the CastResult handler from the SERVER's own zone bounds) now interpolates the effective bite catch zone from the rod's base minigameZoneSize up to new GameConfig.MiniGame.biteZoneCeiling=0.85 (tunable). perfect cast->0.85, good->~0.56/0.62, ok/no-cast->base floor unchanged. The N16 re-roll stays as the security floor (always-hit exploiter capped at the perfect-honest rate, never 100%; rarity/value remain server-rolled). Corrected the inaccurate 'honest clients are unaffected' comment. No client protocol change (avoids 0cw.4 client conflict) -- the bite-timing-accuracy-bonus portion of option C is DEFERRED to the option-B server-authoritative marker-protocol follow-up (needs a client timing protocol). title: TASK 14.3: Fix activeBites memory leak on player disconnect
description:
Server stability requirement — long-running servers must not leak per-player state.

## ROOT CAUSE
FishingService stores per-player bite state in a module-level table `activeBites` (src/server/FishingService.lua:22) keyed by Player instance. Entries are created on Cast (line 72) and removed on SubmitCatchInput (line 140) or timeout (line 129). But if a player disconnects mid-cast (between Cast and SubmitCatchInput), NOTHING removes activeBites[player]. Because the Player instance is the table KEY, the entry holds a strong reference and the Player object is never garbage-collected.

## IMPACT
Memory leak proportional to disconnected-mid-cast players. On a busy server with players leaving frequently, this accumulates. Worse, if a player rejoins, a stale activeBites entry from their PREVIOUS session could theoretically confuse the new session's Cast handler (though in practice session.casting guards against this).

## FIX RECIPE
Two options; implement BOTH for defense-in-depth:

1. In FishingService.init, add a Players.PlayerRemoving listener:

    Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(function(player)
        activeBites[player] = nil
    end)

2. Store bite state on the session object instead of a module-level table (session.activeBite = {...}), which gets cleaned up automatically by DataManager.remove(). This is the cleaner long-term fix but requires touching more code.

RECOMMENDED: Option 1 now (5 lines, zero risk), consider Option 2 as part of the EPIC 12 cross-cutting refactor.

## CONSIDERATIONS
- The redundant check `if not player.Parent or not session.player.Parent` at line 81 is related tech debt (player == session.player) — clean that up while in the file.
- The Cast task.delay closure captures `session` strongly; after disconnect the closure still fires once (harmless, just sets session.casting=false on a dead session table). Not a leak, but worth noting.

## FILES

title: TASK 14.6: Prevent selling fish from a LOCKED aquarium (lock bypass)
description:
PRD AQUA lock mechanic: locked aquariums block ALL theft and modification.

## ROOT CAUSE
FishInventoryService.SellFish (src/server/FishInventoryService.lua:41-88) searches session.carried first, then falls through to session.profile.Aquarium.StoredFish (lines 56-61) WITHOUT checking session.lockedUntil. title: TASK 14.7: Derive aquarium capacity from UpgradeLevel, not persisted field
description:
Data integrity — capacity should be a function of upgrade tier, not a free-floating persisted value.

## ROOT CAUSE
StateSync.getCapacity (src/server/StateSync.lua:7-9) returns session.profile.Aquarium.Capacity directly. There's no enforcement that Capacity matches the player's Aquarium.UpgradeLevel via GameConfig.AquariumUpgradeTiers. A tampered or corrupted profile could have Capacity=999 while UpgradeLevel=1.

## IMPACT
Profile tampering could inflate aquarium capacity, bypassing the upgrade progression. Low likelihood (requires DataStore write access, which exploiters don't have on Roblox) but violates the server-authoritative principle.

## FIX RECIPE
In src/server/StateSync.lua, change getCapacity to derive from the tier table:

    function StateSync.getCapacity(session)
        local level = session.profile.Aquarium.UpgradeLevel or 1
        local tier = GameConfig.AquariumUpgradeTiers[level]
        return tier and tier.capacity or GameConfig.Aquarium.baseCapacity
    end

Then REMOVE the Capacity field from PlayerProfile.default() and the sanitize path (or keep it as a cache that's validated on load against the tier table).

## CONSIDERATIONS
- GameConfig.AquariumUpgradeTiers is currently DEAD CONFIG (see TASK 14.9) — this task activates it. Dependency: should land after or alongside 14.9.
- The incomeMultiplier field on tiers is NOT yet consumed by the income loop — that's separate future work under EPIC 5.
- Removing Capacity from the profile is a schema change; if PlayerProfile.CURRENT_VERSION bumps, migration must handle old saves that HAVE the field (just ignore it on load).
